featured_reviews.review_text:
Malgudi is a South Indian restaurant, but not your typical one. It has a unique spark that makes it stand out. Their innovative mocktail menu immediately caught my attention, and the food selection is extensive, with each dish well described. You’ll even find creative fusions like filter coffee panna cotta and The South Khow Suey.

Food and Drinks
- I tried the Zendo mocktail, which looked stunning with its purple top layer and white base. Each sip revealed a distinct taste as the layers blended.
- The Butter Pepper Garlic Water Chestnut was my absolute favorite. Even though I usually prefer non-vegetarian dishes, this preparation was so flavorful that I’d return just for it.
- The Sri Lankan Tamil Curry, rich with coconut and vegetables, reminded me of Thai curry but with a South Indian twist. It was beautifully paired with idiyappam.
- The Paneer Nellore Biryani was delightful, though I felt it could be improved with a lighter hand on the oil.

Ambience and Service

featured_reviews.name: Ayush Bhandari
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re looking for a spot where traditional South Indian soul meets a modern, aesthetic vibe, Malgudi in Lower Parel is a masterclass in culinary harmony. Curated by the legendary Shankar Mahadevan, the restaurant feels less like a typical eatery and more like a carefully composed melody—vibrant, comforting, and full of character.
The ambience hits you first; it’s thoughtfully designed with a clean, aesthetic appeal that makes it perfect for a relaxed weekend brunch or a stylish dinner.
The Food: From Classic to Creative
The menu takes you on a journey through Karnataka and beyond, elevating humble staples into gourmet experiences.
Podi Cheese Balls: The spice of the podi cuts through the richness of the cheese, creating a crunchy, gooey delight that’s hard to stop at just one.
Ghee Podi Thate Idli: This was a standout. The idli was incredibly soft, acting as the perfect canvas for the fragrant, nutty podi and a generous dousing of ghee.
Davangere Benne Podi Dosa: True to its roots, this dosa was buttery (*benne*) and crisp, with the podi adding a layer of depth that reminded us why this regional specialty is so iconic.
Mulbagal Legacy Cheese Masala Dosa: The addition of cheese modernized the legacy recipe without overshadowing the traditional masala. Beverages:
Mango Berry Matcha: A vibrant, fruity twist on matcha that felt light and refreshing—a great palate cleanser between the buttery dosas.
Coconut Cold Brew Coffee: Smooth and tropical. The natural sweetness of the coconut milk paired beautifully with the bold kick of the cold brew.
Desserts:
You cannot leave without trying the Filter Kaffi Panna Cotta. It’s a brilliant nod to South Indian coffee culture, with a silky texture and a deep caffeine punch. The Chocolate Pull-Up Cake added a bit of "Instagrammable" drama to the table—decadent, rich, and the perfect end for any chocolate lover.

Malgudi isn't just about the name behind it; the food truly speaks for itself. It captures the "Legacy" of South India while dressing it up for the modern Lower Parel.

I recently visited Radhe Shyam Hotel to order food for takeaway, and the entire experience was disappointing.

When I first went to the counter to place my order, I was told to go to another counter because takeaway orders were handled there. At that counter, there wasn't even a proper menu available. Instead, I was handed a photocopied menu, which felt quite unprofessional.

After deciding what to order, I was then told to go back to the first counter to make the payment. At that point, I genuinely felt like I was playing "counter to counter" instead of ordering food.

After paying, I waited for about 10 minutes and asked about the status of my order. The staff member simply said, "Sir, time lagega," which was fine. However, he then told me, "Aap bahar khade raho" in a rude and arrogant manner. He repeated this twice, which made me feel unwelcome as a customer.

Good food alone is not enough—customer service matters too. The lack of coordination, poor ordering process, and disrespectful attitude of the staff completely ruined the experience for me.

I collected my order and left, but unfortunately, I won't be visiting this place again.

After reading some of the other reviews, I guess I should consider myself lucky that the food turned out to be good and safe to eat. That's the only reason I'm giving this place an extra star. Otherwise, based on the service experience alone, it would have been a 1-star review.

Overall, Banana Leaf delivers excellent food with authentic flavors, making it a good choice for South Indian cuisine lovers. Visited Oye Kake at Lower Parel (Kamala Mills) today 🍽️
Honestly, the food is worth trying 👍
The highlights for me were the lassi 🥤 and kulcha 🫓 — both were really good and fresh.
We initially wanted to try the Katahal Biryani, but it wasn’t available due to a gas issue 😅
Instead, we went for Amritsari Pulao — tasted good, simple and satisfying 🙂
Special mention to Ankush More (restaurant manager) for personally guiding us with the menu and helping us choose the right dishes 🙌
Overall, a good experience. Would definitely visit again — hopefully next time for that Katahal Biryani 🤞😄

featured_reviews.name: Devendra Ghogale (Dev)
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re craving authentic North Indian flavors with a homely touch, Oye Kaka is a place you shouldn’t miss. The vibe is simple yet inviting, making it perfect for a relaxed meal with friends or family.
The highlight here is definitely the rich and flavorful gravies — their butter chicken and dal makhani stand out with just the right balance of spices and creaminess. The kebabs are well-cooked and juicy, adding a great start to the meal. Pair it all with soft, freshly made rotis or naan, and you’re sorted.
Portion sizes are generous, and the pricing feels reasonable for the quality served. Service is quick and friendly, though it can get a bit busy during peak hours.
Overall, Oye Kaka delivers comfort food that hits the spot — a solid choice when you’re in the mood for hearty Punjabi cuisine. Do order their Kulchas and karare bhendi as per pics..follow for for more reviews.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Hello Devendra,
It's delightful to hear that you enjoyed the authentic North Indian flavors at Oye Kaka! The butter chicken and dal makhani really are favorites among our guests, and it's fantastic to know they hit the mark for you. We're passionate about providing a welcoming atmosphere for friends and family to gather and share a wonderful meal together.  We look forward to welcoming you back soon! 


Regards,
Team Oye Kake.

I went to Oye Kake recently and loved the food! I tried Lasooni Chaap, Malai Chaap, Cheese Kulcha, Paneer Rogan, and Naanizza — everything tasted amazing.

The chaaps were soft and full of flavour, the cheese kulcha was rich and tasty, and the paneer rogan had perfect spices. The naanizza was a nice twist — crispy and cheesy!

featured_reviews.name: Satyan Soni
featured_reviews.review_text:
An authentic and refined North Indian dining experience.

​We had a lovely dining experience at Oye Kake. The ambiance is elegant and perfectly suited for a quiet family meal.
​The menu delivers beautifully on traditional flavors. While the chaat didn't quite hit the mark for us, the starters, mains, and desserts were top-notch. Their mains veg paired with perfectly textured Chur Chur Naan was a delightful combination that everyone thoroughly enjoyed. And you simply cannot leave without ordering the Kulhad Malai Lassi—it is spectacular.
​Great food, warm hospitality, and a lovely atmosphere for families.

We look forward to welcoming you back soon!

Team Oye Kake.

featured_reviews.name: Khushpreet Kaur Pannu
featured_reviews.review_text:
I went here with my colleagues and it turned out to be such a wonderful experience!

The entire space is beautifully designed around authentic Punjab culture — from the decor to the seating arrangement, everything gives you complete Punjabi vibes. The ambience feels warm, lively, and very positive.

The food was absolutely amazing — rich in taste and truly authentic.

The staff was very polite, calm, and welcoming, which made the experience even better. Service was impressively quick, even though the place is quite spacious.

Overall, a perfect place for team lunches, family outings, or simply enjoying authentic Punjabi food in a vibrant setting. Definitely worth visiting!
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Hello Khushpreet,
Creating memorable experiences is what we aim for, and it’s wonderful to hear you and your colleagues enjoyed the ambiance and authentic flavors of Punjab. The attention to decor and atmosphere is designed to reflect the rich culture, and it seems we hit the mark!  We look forward to welcoming you back soon! 


Regards,
Team Oye Kake.

featured_reviews.name: Kaajal Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently dined at Oye Kake in Lower Parel, and it was a delightful experience! The restaurant has a vibrant, Punjabi-themed ambiance that immediately sets a fun and welcoming tone. The menu offers a wide range of North Indian dishes, and the food is absolutely delicious.

The portion sizes are generous, and the flavors are authentic. The service was quick, and the staff was friendly, making the entire experience even better.

Whether you’re in the mood for a hearty meal or just some good old comfort food, Oye Kake is definitely worth a visit. I highly recommend it for anyone craving some genuine North Indian cuisine in Lower Parel.

featured_reviews.name: Joyreet Das
featured_reviews.review_text:
We stopped by Shree Sunders in Lower Parel for a quick dinner after a shopping spree at Phoenix Palladium, and it turned out to be a great choice for some comforting North Indian food.

Ordered the Butter Kulcha with Chole Masala, which was really tasty. The kulcha was soft and buttery, and the chole had a rich, satisfying flavour. A simple meal but done very well. 9/10.

Service was quick and friendly, which made the experience even better after a long evening of shopping. Definitely a good spot if you’re around the mall and craving North Indian comfort food.

featured_reviews.name: Bhaskar A
featured_reviews.review_text: Shree Sundar has changed their name now it is known has Tamarind Tiffin by Sunders. The Taste and service is same as it is it never changed keep it up. There is parking shortage but the ambience and atmosphere is like meditation peace ✌🏻 value for money.

featured_reviews.name: Roslin Dwivedi
featured_reviews.review_text: We enjoyed a very delicious dinner here. It was Sunday, so the restaurant was packed. We had to wait for a while before getting a table. The place is small but doesn’t give off a too-crammed feeling. It’s clean. The staff are good at their work, and the food is very good. I was surprised by the quality of food and how quickly it came given the restaurant was full. One more thing I noticed is that the menu has so much variety and almost everything sounds good. We ordered at least 3-4 times for 3 of us and enjoyed eating everything we ordered.

featured_reviews.name: Meghna
featured_reviews.review_text:
Food was good but high price for fast food restaurant. It should be bit reasonable I feel. Approx 600/- per person.

Dahi puri had bit sour dahi. And chole pindi was less flavourfull. Overall good. Maybe its good for south indian food which Im yet to try.

I had dahi puri, chole, lacha paratha, butter roti, dum alu kashmiri, veg lasagne.

Service was good. Personal care was taken with regards to service. They have parking space too.

featured_reviews.name: Nidhi Tamboli
featured_reviews.review_text: We had a wonderful experience at Shree Sundar South Indian Restaurant. We tried Ghee Podi Dosa, Spring Dosa, Masala Dosa, and Pineapple Sheera, and everything tasted absolutely delicious. The dosas were crisp, flavorful, and well-prepared, while the pineapple sheera was perfectly balanced with sweetness and freshness. The service was prompt and attentive, and the overall ambiance was comfortable for a relaxed meal. Definitely a great place for authentic and tasty South Indian food — highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Sanoop Kannur
featured_reviews.review_text: Decent pure vegetarian restaurant in Lower Parel with a good mix of South Indian, North Indian, and some continental options. Food taste and quality are satisfactory, and the place is clean with prompt service. However, prices feel on the higher side for basic/casual items—e.g., ₹310 for Roasted Tomato Soup, ₹510 for Delhi Paneer Butter Masala, ₹250 for Jeera Rice, and ₹130 for filter coffee. Total bill around ₹2,255 for a simple family meal (photo attached). Typical premium for the location near Phoenix Mall, but may not offer the best value if you're budget-conscious
